questions.text: "The ___ of resources between rich and poor nations has become more unequal." (distribute → noun)
"___ in renewable energy has increased rapidly." (invest → noun)
"An ___ studies the economy and advises governments." (economy → person)
"___ housing policies make accommodation accessible to low-income families." (afford → adjective)
"High ___ rates mean many workers cannot find jobs." (employ → negative noun)
"___ economics studies how individual firms and consumers make decisions." (micro-)
"The currency was ___ — it was worth less than its official rate implied." (under-)
questions.hint: under- + valued = undervalued (lower than true value)

questions.text: "Income grew ___ during the decade." (significant → adverb)
"Strong ___ between firms keeps prices low." (compete → noun)
"The government decided to ___ the nationalised industry." (private → verb: privatise)
questions.hint: private → privatise (-ise suffix: to make private)

questions.text: What is a "market failure"?
opts: When unregulated markets produce socially suboptimal outcomes
questions.correct: When unregulated markets produce socially suboptimal outcomes

questions.text: "An ___ market makes no regulations, which can cause externalities." (regulate → negative adjective)
"The ___ of wages is fiercely debated." (regulate → noun)
"Countries with poor infrastructure are often ___ economically." (under- + develop → adjective)
What is "negative equity" in property?
opts: When a mortgage is worth more than the property
When property prices are falling rapidly
When interest rates exceed income growth
When rent is higher than mortgage payments
questions.correct: When a mortgage is worth more than the property

questions.text: "___ taxation taxes higher incomes at higher rates." (progress → adjective)
questions.hint: progress → progressive (-ive suffix: relating to progress/increase)

questions.text: "___ behaviour — like present bias — can lead to poor financial decisions." (ir- + rational → adjective)
"The ___ of wealth across generations is one reason inequality persists." (inherit → noun)
questions.hint: inherit → inheritance (-ance suffix: the process/result of inheriting)

questions.text: What is the "lemon problem" in economics?
opts: Too many low-quality lemons in food markets
Information asymmetry drives out high-quality sellers, leaving mainly low-quality goods
A surplus of any good that becomes worthless
The difficulty of pricing unique or rare goods
questions.correct: Information asymmetry drives out high-quality sellers, leaving mainly low-quality goods
questions.hint: Reading 1: "lemon problem… drives out sellers of high-quality cars"

questions.text: "The government plans to ___ the sector — removing many existing rules." (de- + regulate)", (deregulate)
"She is ___ — she has a job, but it is far below her skill level." (under-)
The interest calculated on both the original sum and all accumulated interest is called ___ interest.
"A ___ economy grows in a way that can be maintained for future generations." (sustain → adjective)
"Economic" (relating to the economy) and "economical" (cost-saving) are interchangeable.
questions.hint: "Economic" = relating to the economy; "economical" = thrifty/cost-saving — different meanings

questions.text: What is "fiat money"?
opts: Currency with no intrinsic value, accepted by government decree
questions.correct: Currency with no intrinsic value, accepted by government decree
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Prof. Sato explains fiat money
